title: Zuckerberg's 6500-Word AI Manifesto Becomes a Target

content_html:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a 6500-word long article titled "The Future Belongs to Everyone" on August 10, systematically elaborating on the vision of "personal superintelligence." He argued that superintelligence should not be concentrated in the hands of a few institutions but distributed to every individual, achieving safety and prosperity through the balance of interests among individuals. The article envisions a future where everyone will have a Ph.D.-level, infinitely patient personalized AI mentor and a superintelligent lawyer. It also promises free or low-cost AI tools to billions of people, while high-computation users would pay through a dynamic auction mechanism.

However, TechCrunch published a comment article directly pointing out that this declaration actually exposes the core dilemma the tech industry faces in promoting AI accessibility — the lack of public trust. The commentary argues that when Zuckerberg outlined an ideal future, he deliberately avoided the real-world harms already caused by AI, and this selective blindness only exacerbates rather than alleviates public anxiety.

The huge gap between an ideal vision and a harsh reality

Take the education scenario as an example, it points out that the AI personalized tutor products described by Zuckerberg already exist — ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all have the ability to assist learning. However, in practice, these tools are mainly used by students to write homework and papers, and due to the lack of a reliable watermark system, teachers cannot distinguish which content is generated by AI. When Zuckerberg describes the future of AI in education, he almost completely ignores such negative impacts that have already occurred. The refusal of one of the most powerful tech leaders in the world to acknowledge these real problems can easily make the public feel uneasy.

The legal scenario also has its controversies. Zuckerberg believes that everyone having a superintelligent lawyer will improve judicial fairness, but TechCrunch questions that AI could also create a large number of fraudulent lawsuits, increasing the complexity of the legal system. In terms of business model, the idea of dynamically auctioning computing power is not new, but if it directly affects the AI usage price for ordinary users, it may lead to a poor experience similar to dynamic price hikes.

Recent surveys show that 64% of Americans believe social media is harmful. Just a week before the declaration was released, a court had already fined Meta $567 million for harming children. The commentary pointed out that Zuckerberg's declaration spent a large portion of its content discussing the vague concept of "intelligence," and his way of argumentation is reminiscent of past ambiguous arguments about freedom of speech. Facebook, as a product, and Zuckerberg, as an individual, are not highly recognized among the American public. The controversies accumulated during the social media era are the root cause of current public anxiety about the impact of AI.

The declaration did not even acknowledge the trust deficit and try to repair it, but instead repeatedly showed how trust was lost in the first place. For tech companies to promote widespread acceptance of AI, they need not only to explain what value AI can create, but also to directly address its potential risks — precisely the part that Zuckerberg chose to avoid.

content_html_zh:
Meta首席执行官马克·扎克伯格8月10日发表了一篇题为《未来属于每个人》的6500字长文，系统阐述了“个人超级智能”的愿景。 他认为，超级智能不应该集中在少数机构手中，而应该分配给每个人，通过个人之间的利益平衡实现安全和繁荣。 文章设想了一个未来，每个人都将拥有一位博士级别的、无限耐心的个性化人工智能导师和一位超级智能的律师。 它还承诺向数十亿人提供免费或低成本的人工智能工具，而高计算力用户将通过动态拍卖机制付费。

然而，TechCrunch发表评论文章直接指出，这一声明实际上暴露了科技行业在推动人工智能可及性方面面临的核心困境——缺乏公众信任。 评论认为，扎克伯格在描绘理想未来时，刻意回避了人工智能已经对现实世界造成的伤害，而这种选择性失明只会加剧而不是缓解公众的焦虑。

理想愿景与严酷现实之间的巨大差距

以教育场景为例，指出扎克伯格描述的AI个性化导师产品已经存在——ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini都具备辅助学习的能力。 但在实践中，这些工具主要被学生用来写作业和论文，由于缺乏可靠的水印系统，教师无法区分哪些内容是由人工智能生成的。 当扎克伯格描述人工智能在教育领域的未来时，他几乎完全忽略了已经发生的这种负面影响。 世界上最强大的科技领导者之一拒绝承认这些真正的问题很容易让公众感到不安。

法律方案也存在争议。 扎克伯格认为，每个人拥有一名超级智能律师将提高司法公正性，但 TechCrunch 质疑人工智能也可能制造大量欺诈性诉讼，增加法律体系的复杂性。 从商业模式来看，动态拍卖算力的想法并不新鲜，但如果直接影响普通用户的AI使用价格，可能会导致类似动态涨价的糟糕体验。

最近的调查显示，64% 的美国人认为社交媒体有害。 就在该声明发布前一周，法院已因伤害儿童而对 Meta 处以 5.67 亿美元的罚款。 评论指出，扎克伯格的声明用很大一部分内容讨论了“情报”这个模糊的概念，他的论证方式让人想起过去关于言论自由的模糊论点。 Facebook作为产品，扎克伯格作为个人，在美国公众中的认可度并不高。 社交媒体时代积累的争议是当前公众对人工智能影响感到焦虑的根源。

该声明甚至没有承认信任赤字并试图修复它，而是一再表明信任是如何丧失的。 对于科技公司来说，要促进人工智能的广泛接受，他们不仅需要解释人工智能可以创造什么价值，还需要直接解决其潜在风险——而这正是扎克伯格选择避免的部分。
